summary: Okanogan County DNR lookout: 1934 ground cab, 1966 40-foot timber tower, out of service since 1997 (emergency status), repaired after the 2014 Carlton Complex fire.

facts.design: 40-foot timber tower with 14 by 14 foot DNR flat-gable cab (1966); the 1934 L-4 ground cab preceded it
facts.status_note: Out of service since 1997 (emergency status); repairs after the 2014 fire kept the tower standing.

staffing.status: last staffed under a DNR contract until July 1997; WillhiteWeb says it is used only occasionally today

access.note: the summit is reached across private land; TrailChick says going up without landowner permission is trespassing

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb describes a drive-up gravel road from Brewster with a gate and No Trespass signs; TrailChick lists a 9.8-mile round trip and says the only public route ends before the summit

corrections.proposed: 40-foot timber tower with 14 by 14 foot DNR flat-gable cab (1966); the L-4 was the 1934 ground cab
corrections.why: NHLR and FireLookout.com describe the standing tower as the 1966 40-foot timber tower with a DNR cab. The L-4 was the earlier ground cab that preceded it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, FireLookout.com and TrailChick give 40 feet (12.2 m); WillhiteWeb gives 60 feet. The record keeps 12.2 m.
NHLR gives 3,760 ft (1,146 m); WillhiteWeb, FireLookout.com and TrailChick give 3,852 ft. The record's 1,146 m follows NHLR. Elevation is not used in the story.
NHLR credits the State Division of Forestry; WillhiteWeb and TrailChick credit the Forest Service. The story reports both.

WillhiteWeb says the fire overran the tower; TrailChick says the lookout was spared. The 1985 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts says the flames moved toward Knowlton Knob without saying the tower burned.
FireLookout.com says the contractor staffed the tower until July 1997; TrailChick says the contractor kept staffing it over the years. Not resolved.
The FFLA Washington chapter report says an unknown benefactor repaired the legs; TrailChick says DNR crews and private landowners did. Not resolved.

WillhiteWeb calls it a drive-up gravel road from Brewster; TrailChick says the public route ends before the summit and that the summit is reached across private land. The record's access level is set to permission.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'unidentified benefactor' claim is supported by the FFLA Washington 2014 chapter report, so it is kept, but the sources disagree on who made the repairs. The brief's design 'L-4' was the 1934 ground cab; the standing 1966 tower is a 40-foot timber tower with a DNR cab, so the design is corrected. The 60-foot figure in WillhiteWeb is the outlier. Staffing after 1997 is contested between FireLookout.com and TrailChick. The brief's elevation of 1,146 m follows NHLR; the other three sources give 3,852 ft (about 1,174 m). The access level is set to permission because the summit route is across private land and the sources disagree on the drive. No photos added; TrailChick and the Forest Lookouts page carry photo captions but no image URLs were read. The chapter report's exact title is inferred from its file name (cr-ewa-2014.pdf); check it before publishing. Confidence medium.
